name: es32-geometry-shaders
title: Geometry shaders: amplification, adjacency, invocations
summary: Four 3D scenes drawn by geometry shaders: 151 points become camera-facing sphere impostors (amplification, gl_PrimitiveIDIn), an icosphere's 80 triangles become prisms (cap strip + side strips separated by EndPrimitive, gl_PrimitiveID to the fragment shader), a torus drawn with TRIANGLES_ADJACENCY gets silhouette outlines, and layout(invocations = 6) places six copies of one cube (gl_InvocationID). Data travels VS -> GS -> FS in interface blocks. Every unambiguous pixel of all four scenes is compared with a CPU model that re-implements the shaders and rasterizes their output; the geometry shader output is captured with transform feedback and compared bit for bit (the exact model uses dyadic data); the adjacency vertex order of LINES_ADJACENCY, LINE_STRIP_ADJACENCY and TRIANGLES_ADJACENCY is read back through gl_VertexID; program queries, MAX_GEOMETRY_* limits, the 5 x 11 input-type / draw-mode matrix and the geometry-shader link rules are checked.
spec: ES 3.2 §11.3 Geometry Shaders: §11.3.1 Input Primitives (the five input types, mismatch rule), §11.3.2 Output Primitives (max_vertices, GEOMETRY_* queries), §11.3.3 Variables, §11.3.4 Execution Environment (§11.3.4.2 Instanced Geometry Shaders and output order, §11.3.4.3 Inputs and gl_PrimitiveIDIn, §11.3.4.4 Outputs and gl_PrimitiveID, §11.3.4.6 Primitive Type Mismatches and Drawing Commands)
ES 3.2 §10.1.5 Triangle Strips, §10.1.8 Lines with Adjacency, §10.1.9 Line Strips with Adjacency, §10.1.10 Triangles with Adjacency (vertex order and ignored trailing vertices)

ES 3.2 §7.3 Program Objects (LinkProgram failure conditions for geometry shaders), §7.4.1 Shader Interface Matching, §7.12 Program Queries (GEOMETRY_VERTICES_OUT / INPUT_TYPE / OUTPUT_TYPE / SHADER_INVOCATIONS and their INVALID_OPERATION rule)

ES 3.2 §11.1.2.1 Output Variables (TransformFeedbackVaryings: geometry shader outputs, block members named Block.member), §12.1 The Last Vertex Processing Stage, §12.2 / §12.2.2 Transform Feedback and Table 12.1 (mode compared with the output type of the geometry shader), §12.3 Primitive Queries (PRIMITIVES_GENERATED), Table 12.3 (provoking vertex)
ES 3.2 Table 21.47 Implementation Dependent Geometry Shader Limits, Table 21.40 (SUBPIXEL_BITS), §9.8 / §11.3.4.5 (LAYER_PROVOKING_VERTEX query)

GLSL ES 3.20 §4.4.1 Input Layout Qualifiers (Geometry Inputs: points, lines, lines_adjacency, triangles, triangles_adjacency, invocations), §4.4.2 Output Layout Qualifiers (Geometry Outputs: points, line_strip, triangle_strip, max_vertices), §4.3.9 Interface Blocks, §7.1.4 Geometry Shader Special Variables, §7.1.5 gl_PrimitiveID, §8.13 Geometry Shader Functions (EmitVertex, EndPrimitive; numbered 8.16 in the project inventory)

api.glCreateShader: GEOMETRY_SHADER objects for all four scenes and for ~30 small shaders in validate(); compile status of the invalid ones (invocations = MAX + 1 and 0, max_vertices = MAX + 1, gl_in[3] with layout(triangles)) is FALSE
api.glShaderSource: geometry shader sources from files and from generated strings
api.glCompileShader: invocations = MAX_GEOMETRY_SHADER_INVOCATIONS + 1 and = 0 fail to compile (GLSL ES 3.20 §4.4.1); the valid control with invocations = MAX compiles and links
api.glAttachShader: vertex + geometry + fragment programs (and geometry-only variants for the link-rule tests)
api.glLinkProgram: links with a geometry shader; fails for: no input layout, no output type, no max_vertices, no vertex shader (non-separable), max_vertices above the limit, VS/GS block member type mismatch, GS input block without a matching VS output, GS input block array of the wrong size
api.glGetProgramiv: LINK_STATUS; GEOMETRY_VERTICES_OUT (4, 15, 12, 3 for the scenes; 1, 2, 1, 3, 3 for the five small programs), GEOMETRY_INPUT_TYPE (all five types), GEOMETRY_OUTPUT_TYPE, GEOMETRY_SHADER_INVOCATIONS (1, 1, 1, 6) compared with the shader sources; the four pnames on a program without a geometry shader -> INVALID_OPERATION
api.glTransformFeedbackVaryings: geometry shader output block members ('GS_OUT.eye', 'GS_OUT.world', ...) in INTERLEAVED_ATTRIBS mode; the captured words equal the CPU model bit for bit
api.glBeginTransformFeedback: TRIANGLES capture of a GL_POINTS draw whose geometry shader outputs triangle_strip is legal (the output type is compared, section 12.2.2); POINTS and LINES -> INVALID_OPERATION at the draw; POINTS capture of lines_adjacency / triangles_adjacency geometry shaders records the vertices
api.glEndTransformFeedback: ends each capture; the buffer is mapped afterwards
api.glBindBufferBase: TRANSFORM_FEEDBACK_BUFFER index 0 receives the interleaved geometry shader output
api.glBufferData: capture buffer pre-filled with a sentinel (bytes after the expected words stay untouched); vertex, index and adjacency index buffers
api.glMapBufferRange: reads the captured buffer for the bit-exact comparison
api.glGenQueries: two query objects: PRIMITIVES_GENERATED and TRANSFORM_FEEDBACK_PRIMITIVES_WRITTEN
api.glBeginQuery: both targets active at once around every capture
api.glGetQueryObjectuiv: PRIMITIVES_GENERATED equals the number of triangles / points the geometry shader emitted (302, 560, 124, 72, and the adjacency tests) and equals TRANSFORM_FEEDBACK_PRIMITIVES_WRITTEN
api.glEnable: RASTERIZER_DISCARD around captures and the error matrix; DEPTH_TEST and SCISSOR_TEST for the cells
api.glDisable: RASTERIZER_DISCARD afterwards; the offscreen mismatch test then renders pixels
api.glDrawArrays: GL_POINTS (cell A), the 55-pair draw-mode matrix (INVALID_OPERATION exactly for incompatible pairs), the offscreen mismatch draws (no fragment rendered), LINES_ADJACENCY / LINE_STRIP_ADJACENCY / TRIANGLES_ADJACENCY vertex-order captures
api.glDrawElements: TRIANGLES (cells B, D), TRIANGLES_ADJACENCY with an index list holding the neighbour vertices (cell C); pixels and captures compared with the model
api.glGenVertexArrays: five VAOs for the four scenes (the adjacency and triangle index buffers of the torus are separate VAO state)
api.glBindVertexArray: selects the scene's vertex and index sources
api.glVertexAttribPointer: positions, sizes and normals of the scenes; observed through pixels and captured vertices
api.glUniformMatrix4fv: view, projection and view-projection matrices; changing them for the exact capture changes the captured values as modelled
api.glUniform2f: silhouette line half width in NDC (observed: outline pixels)
api.glUniform3f: eye position (silhouette facing decisions) and light directions
api.glUniform4fv: u_place[6] of the instanced geometry shader (the six copies move as modelled)
api.glUniform2fv: u_spin[6] (cos, sin) of the six copies
api.glClear: per cell colour and depth clear under a scissor rectangle
api.glGenRenderbuffers: 16x16 RGBA8 target of the mismatch test
api.glFramebufferRenderbuffer: colour attachment of the mismatch test framebuffer; complete
api.glReadPixels: cell readback (through demo::read_rgba8) for the pixel comparison and the 16x16 mismatch test
api.glGetIntegerv: MAX_GEOMETRY_* limits compared with ES 3.2 Table 21.47, MAX_FRAGMENT_INPUT_COMPONENTS, LAYER_PROVOKING_VERTEX is one of the three legal values

visual_review.notes: Viewed the gpu es-max capture (256x256). Top left: a three-armed spiral galaxy of about 150 shaded colour spheres (red, yellow, green, cyan, violet, pink) around a bright central bulge on a navy background, nearer spheres overlapping farther ones with correct occlusion. Top right: an icosphere whose faces have grown into prisms of three heights, each face its own palette colour with lit and shadowed sides and visible depth, on a purple background. Bottom left: a teal Blinn-Phong torus seen from above with a continuous thin yellow outline along its silhouette, outer rim and inner hole, none across the shaded surface. Bottom right: six cubes in a ring (red, orange, green, teal, violet, pink), each with three face brightnesses, on a brown background.
